classification.difficultyReason: Form a quadratic product model, solve an inclusive inequality using its zeroes and sign, then enumerate distinct integer pairs.

content.prompt: Two positive numbers have a sum of 30. Let one of the numbers be $x$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find an expression for the product $P$ of the two numbers.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the values of $x$ for which $P\ge 200$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}30x-x^2&\ge200\\x^2-30x+200&\le0\\(x-10)(x-20)&\le0\end{align*}$$
The zeroes are 10 and 20. The upward-opening parabola $y=(x-10)(x-20)$ is below the $x$-axis between these zeroes and equals zero at them. Hence $10\le x\le20$, which satisfies $0<x<30$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: List the distinct pairs of integers that have a sum of 30 and a product of at least 200.

answer.worked:
From part b, both integers lie between 10 and 20 inclusive. Taking the smaller integer from 10 to 15 avoids counting a pair twice.
$$\begin{align*}10\times20&=200\\11\times19&=209\\12\times18&=216\\13\times17&=221\\14\times16&=224\\15\times15&=225\end{align*}$$
Thus the distinct pairs are $(10,20)$, $(11,19)$, $(12,18)$, $(13,17)$, $(14,16)$ and $(15,15)$.
